predecessors.name: Ikhshidid dynasty
predecessors.text: Mecca, where in about 964 'the Egyptian ruler Abu al-Misk Kafur installed a Meccan sharif as emir to improve pilgrim safety'

successors.name: Kingdom of Hejaz
successors.text: the Hejaz: in June 1916 'Hussein bin Ali, Sharif of Mecca, took the title of king of the Hejaz' as the Arab Revolt began on 10 June 1916

ledger.x: c. 967: the sharifate begins. 'c. 964: the Egyptian ruler Abu al-Misk Kafur installed a Meccan sharif as emir to improve pilgrim safety'; the page dates the state from c. 967, when Ja'far ibn Muhammad ruled (967-980); Fatimid suzerainty from the conquest of Egypt in 969. Year dated 'c.' on the page.
c. 1200-1201: the Qatadids take the sharifate. 'Qatadah ibn Idris seized power around 1200 and was recognised as emir by the Ayyubid sultan. His descendants ruled until 1925.'
10 June 1916: the Arab Revolt and the kingdom.

wars.name: Wahhabi conquest of the Hejaz
wars.outcome: 1803 Mecca attacked; Ghalib fled and returned as a Saudi vassal; Taif first, then Mecca and Medina (Diriyah page); 1813 Tusun Pasha took Mecca.

wars.name: Arab Revolt in the Hejaz
wars.outcome: 5 June 1916 the attack on Medina failed; 10 June the revolt was proclaimed at Mecca; Jeddah surrendered on 16 June; Mecca fell on 9 July; Ta'if on 22 September; Rabigh, Yanbu and al Qunfudhah by the end of September; Medina held out until 9 January 1919.

certainty.note: A holy-city emirate with no described boundary on the page: Mecca is firm; the Hejaz limits (Al-'Ula, Al Lith, Khaybar) are the page's for the 19th century only; suzerainty changed repeatedly (Ikhshidid, Fatimid, Sulayhid, Ayyubid…
